title: Settings card: 2024 KTM 250 SX-F
ig_caption:
2024 KTM 250 SX-F. About 195 lb, fast, hardpack moto, stock suspension, stability and jump support the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the standard settings from KTM's 2024 owner's manual for the 250 SX-F and 250 XC-F.

Stock is 12 and 18 on the fork, 15 clicks and 1 1/2 turns on the shock, 15 on shock rebound, 105 mm of riding sag. Dialed went 1 click in on fork comp, 8 in on fork rebound, 5 in on low-speed, a quarter turn in on high-speed and 3 in on shock rebound. Sag stays at 105. Eight clicks is a big move: if the front starts to feel slow or packs in braking bumps, come back toward stock two at a time. Fork air: set it from the manual for your weight.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

250 SX-F riders: where's your fork rebound sitting?

title: Settings card: 2025 Kawasaki KX450
ig_caption:
2025 Kawasaki KX450. About 125 lb, fast, rutted clay moto, stock suspension, stability and jump support the goals. Left is stock from the 2025 KX450 owner's manual, right is the baseline Dialed built for that rider.

Fork comp 12 to 14, fork rebound 12 to 13. Shock low-speed 11 to 12, high-speed 2 turns to 1 1/2, rebound 13 to 15. Sag set at 105 mm. A light rider on a big bike gets less compression and a quicker return on most clickers, with half a turn of high-speed in for the landings.

title: Settings card: 2026 Yamaha YZ250F
ig_caption:
2026 Yamaha YZ250F. About 175 lb, learning, hardpack moto, stability and comfort the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the standard settings from the 2026 YZ250F owner's service manual.

Stock is 13 and 12 on the fork, 12 clicks and 1 1/2 turns on the shock, 12 on shock rebound, and Yamaha's 90 to 100 mm sag window. Dialed went 1 click out on fork comp and 2 out on shock rebound, left the other three alone and set sag at 100. For a newer rider on hardpack, stock is already close, and not every click has to move.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

title: Settings card: 2022 Honda CRF250R
ig_caption:
2022 Honda CRF250R. About 195 lb, fast, hardpack moto, stock suspension, stability and jump support the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the standard settings from Honda's CRF250R competition handbook (Honda Motor Europe edition).

Stock is 12 and 13 on the fork, 6 clicks and 2 1/6 turns on the shock, 11 on shock rebound, 105 mm of riding sag. Dialed went 1 click in on fork comp, 3 in on fork rebound, 4 out on low-speed, 5/6 of a turn in on high-speed and 1 out on shock rebound. Sag stays at 105. Low-speed went softer while high-speed went firmer: more grip on the gas, more hold on the big hits.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

title: Settings card: 2027 Yamaha YZ250FX
ig_caption:
2027 Yamaha YZ250FX. About 255 lb, learning, singletrack, stock suspension, stability and comfort the goals. Left is stock from the 2027 YZ250FX owner's service manual, right is the baseline Dialed built for that rider.

Fork comp 7 to 13, fork rebound 7 to 12. Shock low-speed 10 to 12, high-speed 1 5/8 turns to 1 3/8, rebound 10 to 13. Sag 100 mm, the top of Yamaha's 90 to 100 window. Comfort and a newer rider drove it: compression and rebound came out, with a quarter turn of high-speed in for the big hits. Six clicks is a big move, so if it starts to bottom, come back toward stock two at a time.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.
